notes.summary: Actual geometric finite pullback is reconstructed on primary models; full positive descent applies to injections, while noninjective maps only factor over their exact image.
notes.detailedSummary: The source blowup is closed in finite base change by a graded Rees surjection. Actual Cartier effectivity, contracted-curve degrees and support-quotient evaluation prove geometric pullback. Qualified G331 supplies full C/D descent, including conductor-infinite, nonminimal and partial-bottom fibres. No ambient extension theorem follows from exact-image factorization.
notes.text:
Use only the entire qualified G331 and G345, preserving their complete source/scope qualifications. Let R be excellent reduced local, a proper primary gauge, and X_R the FULL centred section v(a)=1. For finite reduced B, use the disjoint union of closed-centre sections in the extended gauge aB. Positive lower-dimensional centres remain; zero-dimensional centres have empty sections.

C and D are G331's independently geometric continuous class and actual decreasing-C-net completion. Their ideal comparisons are granted comparison theorems, not definitions replacing geometry. G345 supplies the independently geometric bounded D product of arity dim R−1, supported Cartier comparison, ordinary OPEN locality and uniform weak/prescribed-D-limit decreasing-NET continuity. Neither grant supplies general envelope regularization or energy.

For primary I, multiplication gives a graded surjection Rees_R(I)⊗_R B→Rees_B(IB), degree r having image I^rB=(IB)^r. Relative Proj therefore embeds the ACTUAL source blowup as a CLOSED subscheme of finite base change, hence maps finitely to the base model. Equality with unrestricted base change is not asserted. A surviving positive-dimensional source component cannot map wholly to the closed point, since it would then be finite over a field and zero-dimensional. Base exceptional Cartier equations are units at all surviving source generic points and consequently regular on the reduced source model. Actual effective constituents pull back effectively.

A contracted integral source curve maps finitely to an integral base curve. Its pulled bundle degree over the base residue field is the image degree times the full function-field degree. Intrinsic source-residue-field degree divides this by its positive closed residue degree. Nonnegative curve degrees therefore survive. At a semivaluation with support Q, evaluation pulls the same invertible lattice with generic trivialization to the valuation ring of Frac(B/Q); composition gives the base centre and identical value. No total-fraction-ring map into a nonminimal support quotient is presumed. This proves core pullback geometrically; ideal extension, uniform limits and actual decreasing representations preserve C/D.

For an injection, G331 gives a compact surjective restriction rho and rho* K_R={H∈K_B constant on EVERY full rho-fibre}, K=C,D. This includes conductor-infinite, mixed-zero, nonminimal and partial-bottom cases. Normalization fibres are singletons at finite conductor value and precisely conductor-quotient fibres at infinite value; the finite stratum is open and the infinite stratum closed.

For a noninjection, A=R/ker(R→B) is reduced and X_A={v∈X_R:v(ker)=∞} is the closed exact image. The injection A→B has the preceding descent theorem. Restriction K_R→K_A preserves actual representations but need not be onto, as n4 proves. Empty-fibre supremum −∞ and infimum zero are order conventions, not geometric membership assertions. Bottom remains in D but is outside bounded product inputs.

notes.summary: Raw envelopes have a universal fibre-admissible identity and unrestricted inequality, with exact conditional positivity transfer.
notes.detailedSummary: For bounded obstacles and K=C or D, full positive descent bijects the constrained competitor sets. No arbitrary supremum membership, USC regularization or increasing closure is assumed. An admissible unrestricted upstairs envelope commutes exactly when it is full-fibre constant.
notes.text:
For K=C,D and bounded finite f define P_R^Kf(v)=sup{u(v):u∈K_R,u≤f}. A sufficiently negative reference constant is a competitor, so the raw envelope is finite and nonpositive. Its K membership and regularity are not assumed.

For an injection, constrain upstairs competitors to be constant on EVERY full fibre. N1 gives an order bijection with downstairs competitors. Pointwise evaluation proves P_(B,fib)^K(f∘rho)=rho*P_R^Kf and P_B^K(f∘rho)≥rho*P_R^Kf. This uses independently geometric positivity descent rather than a formal completion definition.

The constrained envelope belongs to K_B exactly when the downstairs envelope belongs to K_R: pullback proves one direction, and full descent of the fibre-constant function proves the other. If the unrestricted upstairs envelope itself belongs to K_B, unrestricted equality is equivalent to its full-fibre constancy. For sufficiency descend it to h∈K_R; surjectivity gives h≤f, so h is a downstairs competitor. Necessity follows because a pullback is fibre constant. An unknown raw supremum is never inserted as an admissible competitor.

For a noninjection the exact constrained identity uses A=R/ker and f restricted to X_A. Pullback of R competitors still gives the unrestricted inequality. It does not identify P_A(f|X_A) with the restriction of P_Rf. N4 disproves that stronger identity with positive continuous envelopes on both spaces.

notes.text:
Take k=C, R=k[x,y,z]_(x,y,z)/(xy), A1=k[x,z]_(x,z), A2=k[y,z]_(y,z), T=k[z]_(z), and S=A1×A2. Polynomial localization gives excellence, and (xy)=(x)∩(y) gives reduction. Restriction identifies R=A1×_T A2: subtract a common line residue and lift the remaining xa(x,z), yb(y,z) independently; local denominators lift to units. The two idempotents generate S as an R-module. Normality of both component factors proves S is the finite normalization.

Multiplication by (1,0) forces a conductor element's common line residue to vanish, and zero residue is sufficient. Thus c=(x,y), cS=xA1×yA2, R/c=T and S/c=T×T. In the maximal-ideal gauge the only conductor-infinite downstairs point v0 kills (x,y) and induces ord_z. Its support is nonminimal. Its FULL fibre consists of w1 killing x on A1 and w2 killing y on A2, both inducing ord_z: the normalized DVR section of T is a singleton. Finite-conductor fibres are singleton by w(s)=v(cs)−v(c) for finite-valued conductor c.

On ALL X_R set f(v)=−1−1/v(y), with 1/∞=0. Since v(y)∈[1,∞], reciprocal continuity makes f continuous and bounded between −2 and −1. On A1 it is constantly −1. On A2 let o2=ord_(y,z); its graded ring k[y,z] is a domain, so it is a valuation. For EVERY primary J, J⊂(y,z)^o2(J), hence w(J)≥o2(J) for EVERY normalized w. Unit ideals, negative real combinations, uniform C limits and actual decreasing D infima preserve u(w)≤u(o2).

Since f(o2)=−2, every second-plane competitor is at most −2 everywhere. Constant −2 attains it; the first-plane envelope is −1. Both choices simultaneously form the genuine boundary-power ideal (x,z)×(y,z)^2. Therefore the ENTIRE upstairs C and D envelopes are the admissible continuous tuple (−1,−2). Every downstairs competitor pulls to the second plane and has value at most −2 at v0; constant −2 downstairs attains it. Consequently P_R^Cf(v0)=P_R^Df(v0)=−2, and the upstairs-minus-pulled-downstairs gap at w1 is exactly ONE. General downstairs envelope membership is neither needed nor claimed.

The fibre maximum of this tuple is −2 at second-plane monomial valuations w_M(y)=M,w_M(z)=1, but −1 at v0. Lowest y exponents show w_M→w2 pointwise, including local unit denominators. The maximum is discontinuous and its second-plane restriction violates u(w2)≤u(o2), so is not D. Direct tensor calculation gives S⊗_R S=A1×T×T×A2. The vertical T components have nonempty boundaries and cannot be discarded by generic field arguments.

This is a geometric conductor-infinite obstruction, distinct from the curve mixed-zero literal radial obstruction. Artifact: sections/n3.tex.

notes.text:
For EVERY field k let R=k[x,y]_(x,y), Q=R/(xy), with maximal-ideal gauges. R is excellent normal regular of dimension two and Q excellent reduced of dimension one. Q's full boundary consists exactly of wx(x)=1,wx(y)=∞ and wy(x)=∞,wy(y)=1, from its two normalization DVRs. Their restriction is injective with closed two-point image. The ordinary order o on R is a further normalized valuation because gr_m R=k[x,y] is a domain.

The obstacle f(v)=−1/v(x), reciprocal at infinity zero, is continuous on ALL X_R and takes values in [−1,0]. As in n3, J⊂m^o(J) proves u(v)≤u(o) for EVERY C_R/D_R potential and EVERY support. A competitor has u(o)≤−1, hence is at most −1 everywhere. The genuine primary profile −v(m)=−1 attains this. Thus P_R^Cf=P_R^Df=−1 on FULL X_R.

On Q, genuine primary ideals J_N=(x^N,y)Q give −w(J_N)/N=(−1,−1/N), converging uniformly on the entire two-point boundary to h=(−1,0). G331 comparison puts h in C_Q⊂D_Q. It is the restricted obstacle itself, so P_Q^C(f∘rho)=P_Q^D(f∘rho)=h. Both envelopes are actual positive continuous geometric functions, and the gap at wy is ONE. This failure is not an existence gap.

There is no D_R extension of h: a value zero at rho(wy) forces identically zero by G331's normal zero dichotomy, contradicting the −1 value at rho(wx). Fibre constancy on an injective boundary map is therefore insufficient when the ring map is noninjective. Exact-image factorization supplies no ambient extension.

Individual ideals lift to (x^N,y) in R, but their profiles g_N=−min(v(x),v(y)/N) violate the ambient obstacle at o for N>1. They increase to zero where v(y)<∞ and to −1 where v(y)=∞. Along monomial points (1,M) tending to rho(wx), that limit is zero but its endpoint value is −1. It is not USC and therefore not D.

For another primary b, transport functions and obstacles by division by v(b). Competitor sets transport bijectively. The homogeneous obstacle becomes −w(m)^2/w(x), the ambient envelope −w(m), and the gap at the transported y branch is 1/ord_y(bQ)>0.

G345 gives mu_R(−1)=delta_o from the exceptional P1 degree, while mu_Q()=delta_wx+delta_wy from zero-arity DVR degrees. The ambient measure assigns zero to the closed image; the intrinsic curve reference has mass two. Their arities differ. Q has zero fixed ambient degree-two contribution, consistently with n5. notes.text:
Let n=dim R≥1, p=n−1. Define mu_B^[R] as the sum of f_q mu_Bq over closed centres of dimension n, where f_q=[kappa(q):kappa(m)]. These are the already independently geometric G345 operators with p slots. Smaller centres contribute zero ambient degree while keeping their points and potentials. For top minimal P put K_P=Frac(R/P), d_P=dim_KP(B⊗_R K_P), and j_P:X_(R/P)→X_R.

For bounded u1,…,up∈D_R the theorem is rho_*mu_B^[R](rho*u1,…,rho*up)=sum_P d_P j_P,*mu_(R/P)(j_P*u1,…,j_P*up). No injection is required. The same component decomposition for R has coefficients one.

Geometric proof comes FIRST. On a common actual primary model carrying core inputs and an effective exceptional Cartier test, n1 supplies the finite actual source model and regular pulled equations. Each integral top component map is proper dominant with equal delta-dimension n and full field degree [L:K_P]. Excellence gives the universally catenary dimension-function setup. Complete Stacks42.26.3 gives h_*div(h*s)=[L:K_P]div(s) AS ACTUAL CYCLES, before Chow equivalence. Its immediate proof uses the norm/divisor lemma and Nm(g)=g^[L:K_P]; that recursive norm/divisor foundation is disclosed published background. Inseparability is retained. Complete33.45.7 then projects intersections on proper residue-field schemes with residue function-field degrees, or zero for smaller image dimension. G345's m-filtration retains Cartier thicknesses in mixed characteristic. Intrinsic closed-centre degrees convert to base degrees by f_q. Smaller components cannot supply a primary closed-fibre prime of dimension p. These facts give geometric core projection, not a definition by module rank.

For the complete coefficient check let H_M be the ambient degree-n form of the eventual multi-primary length polynomial. Complete current SH17.1.6 and17.4.1–4 were read. Noetherian generation of the multigraded intersection module gives I^sM1⊂I^sM2∩M1⊂I^(s−c)M1 in an exact sequence. The middle quotient length is the difference of the M2/M3 polynomials. Along every positive rational ray the exterior polynomials have identical top form, so squeezing proves H_M2=H_M1+H_M3. No coefficient inequality is inferred from polynomial domination.

A finite prime filtration exists by successive elements with maximal annihilator, which is prime, and Noetherian termination. Only top minimal factors contribute degree n. Reduced R_P is the field K_P; localizing counts precisely d_P factors. Hence H_B=sum_P d_P H_(R/P). The generic reduced algebra is a product of finite fields, so d_P is their FULL degree sum, including inseparability, or zero when absent. For every primary product L, Artinian centre decomposition gives the exact identity length_R(B/LB)=sum_q f_q length_Bq(Bq/LBq). Comparing forms proves every selected mixed coefficient.

With p rational input profiles and a primary test J, G345's exact moments give the measure identity. J=a gives finite mass. The G331 gauge-difference lattice is uniformly dense on FULL X_R, including min(v(g),N)=v((g)+a^N), so all supports are tested. Uniform rational approximation gives C tuples. Actual decreasing C representations of bounded D limits stay in a common [−M,0]; pullback and quotient restriction preserve the known limits. Constant d_P=d gives d mu_R. Normalization has d_P=1 and recovers full closed-residue weighted conductor pushforward; identified masses are added without deleting points or asserting zero capacity. notes.text:
Let A be excellent normal local domain, A⊂B finite domain, fraction fields K⊂L and d=[L:K]. Entire G331 gives the coefficient-norm trace T with finite kernels of mass d and FULL fibre support. Its proof uses generic inseparable lengths, polynomial Gauss minima after support quotient, dense ideal differences and extension of every fibre point. It preserves C; finite nonpositive sums along actual decreasing representations preserve D.

Choose a finite NORMAL splitting field M/K containing L, including inseparable roots, and its finite integral closure E over A. Write G=Aut_K(M), pi:X_E→X_B. Every embedding of L extends to an automorphism of M; the r separable embeddings repeat |G|/r times, while the norm repeats d/r times. Thus rho_E*TH=(d/|G|)sum_g g*pi*H on EVERY support. This does not set [M:K]=|G|. For E/A, G331's full-support kernel makes each entire fibre a G-orbit. Every B fibre point lifts to E.

The finite orbit maximum belongs to C_E or D_E and is full-fibre constant, so positively descends. Its value is exactly M H(v)=max_(rho w=v)H(w). Consequently M preserves C/D. If H≤f∘rho then M H≤f and H≤rho*M H; comparing competitors proves P_B^K(f∘rho)=rho*P_A^Kf, K=C,D, without envelope-membership assumptions. For reduced sources this maximum argument extends when EVERY minimal component dominates A, by quotient restriction and finite maxima. Vertical components are excluded from that conclusion.

For n=dim A≥2, bounded H∈D_B and remaining bounded pulled inputs, rho_*mu_B^[A](H,rho*u2,…)=mu_A(TH,u2,…). Put e=[M:L]. N5 for E/B gives pi_*mu_E^[A](pi*H,rho_E*u2,…)=e mu_B^[A](H,rho*u2,…). Automorphisms preserve geometric products, first by ideal quotient-length isomorphisms and dense tests, then by G345 continuities; they preserve closed residue weights. Every orbit-transformed selected-slot product therefore has equal pushforward to A. Multilinearity in ONE slot turns the orbit trace identity into d times the pushforward with pi*H. The other side, by E/A projection, is ed mu_A(TH,u2,…); E/B projection makes the first side de times the desired source pushforward. Cancel ed>0. T is UNNORMALIZED, so no extra d remains. For p=1 the remaining list is empty; n=1 has no selected slot.

For arbitrary reduced B over normal A, sum traces over dominating minimal domain components and use n5's component decomposition for arbitrary source tuples. Vertical components have zero ambient product but remain in the spaces; this sum trace is not asserted full-support on their fibres.

At an exceptional target DVR Z, finite integral closure in L is free of rank d. Uniformizer reduction proves sum e_Z'/Z f_Z'/Z=d. Smith normal form makes norm order its cokernel length, equal to sum f_Z'/Z ord_Z'(g); uniformizer scaling extends this to rational Cartier equations. Thus core trace evaluation at ord_Z/b_Z is b_Z^−1 sum f_Z'/Z ord_Z'(D). These are proper Weil pushforward coefficients on normalized primary models, unchanged under dominating DVR refinement. A finite Cartier determination downstairs is not claimed. Artifact: sections/n6.tex.

notes.text:

Pull bounded H∈D_B to C. On every normal local centre S_i sum the n6 normal-domain traces over minimal C_i components dominating S_i. Call this T_iH. Each is a bounded geometric D potential, or C for continuous H; finite generic degrees bound the sums. No generic degree is invented for a vertical component.

The EXACT admissibility condition is that the ENTIRE tuple (T_iH) be constant on EVERY full X_S→X_R fibre. This includes conductor-infinite quotient fibres, nonminimal supports, lower centres and centres giving zero ambient mass. Entire G331 then descends it uniquely to T_RH in D_R, or C_R.

Apply n6 on every top S_i, multiply by its exact CLOSED residue degree and push to R. G345 normalization makes the target sum precisely the displayed right side. Every ambient top B component lies above a top minimal R prime: finite dimension equality and an extended prime chain exclude a nonminimal target prime. There S becomes K_P, so C/B has generic degree ONE on EVERY ambient top source component. N5 converts the pulled source component sum into mu_B^[R]. Closed residue degrees multiply identically along the two routes. Lower components keep their points with zero ambient contribution; no zero-capacity assertion follows.

notes.text:
Let B be reduced finite locally free of positive rank d over excellent reduced local R. It is free and faithfully flat. For a global semilocal boundary-power ideal J choose finite R-module generators g_j, h=sum T_jg_j, and write det(t1−m_h)=t^d+sum_i(−1)^i c_i(T)t^(d−i). Let C_i(J) be the genuine coefficient ideals and N_fl(J)=C_d(J).

The determinant is the scalar on the top exterior power of a projective module. Basis conjugation proves independence, matrices prove arbitrary base change, and substitutions between generating families give coefficient containment both ways. Complete current Stacks31.18.6 was read and the construction independently checked. Images generate the extended image ideal without asserting injectivity of its tensor inclusion. If J contains a^NB, add generators x·1_B from a^N; pure norm coefficients x^d show N_fl(J) contains a boundary power. Lesser coefficient ideals need not be primary.

At any base support P use the valued field K_v=Frac(R/P). F=B⊗_R K_v has dimension d and may be NONREDUCED. Split all residue extensions in a finite normal field M and extend the valuation. The Artinian factors have residue M and FULL lengths l_j summing to d. Their maximal-ideal filtrations make multiplication characteristic polynomials (t−h_j)^l_j. These lengths retain fibre nilpotence and inseparable splitting multiplicity. Residue maps give centred source points w_j. Gauss coefficient minimum is multiplicative after quotienting supports, dividing by a least coefficient and reducing nonzero residue polynomials. Hence v(N_fl(J))=sum_j l_j w_j(J).

The finite positive kernel has mass d. Dense full semilocal gauge differences make it choice-independent. Every fibre point's support quotient fraction field is a residue field of F; embed it in M and extend its valuation. It occurs with positive length in that choice and thus in all choices. The kernel has FULL support, and every fibre has at most d points. The trace tau H is continuous on continuous functions by dense tests and the mass bound, sends rational negative profiles to −v(N_fl(J))/q, and consequently preserves C. Finite directed sums of nonpositive values commute with actual decreasing limits, including bottom, producing actual C representations and D preservation.

For maxima let m=min_(rho w=v)w(J), finite because J contains a boundary power. In the Gauss-valued field M(T), all characteristic coefficients have value at least im. If all had strictly greater value, inserting a root of value m into its monic equation would make the leading term uniquely least-valued, impossible. Therefore m=min_i v(C_i(J))/i on EVERY support, with zero ideals valued infinity. Put L=sup_X v(C_d(J))/d<∞ and choose integer N>dL. Since N/i>L, replacing C_i by the genuine PRIMARY-truncated ideal C_i+a^N leaves this minimum EXACTLY unchanged. Thus M(−w(J)/q)=max_i[−v(C_i(J)+a^N)/(qi)] is a genuine rational profile after common denominators and ideal sums.

Uniform 1-Lipschitz contraction of fibre maxima extends this to C. An actual decreasing C_B net has maxima decreasing to its exact maximum on every FINITE fibre: directedness chooses one index for all points, using finite thresholds at bottom. This supplies an actual C_R representation and D membership. N6's competitor argument therefore proves unrestricted RAW envelope equality for reduced finite-flat maps, including nonnormal targets, with membership transfer when known. No arbitrary supremum closure or regularization is used.

For automatic conductor admissibility, base change to every normal S_i. B⊗_R S_i is free rank d; its generic algebra is a reduced localization of B. Nilpotents die generically and therefore vanish by torsion-freeness. Complete Stacks10.39.19 going-down makes every minimal source prime contract to a minimal target prime, so no vertical minimal component occurs. Its immediate localization/faithful-flat prime-lifting background is disclosed. No reduction loses determinant rank.

Determinant base change identifies the pullback of tau H with the sum of normal-domain traces on EVERY S_i support, first for rational profiles, then uniformly and by finite decreasing sums. This tuple is already a full-fibre-constant downstairs pullback. N7 therefore proves rho_*mu_B^[R](H,rho*u2,…)=mu_R(tau H,u2,…). The normalization routes use top generic degree one and multiplying CLOSED residue weights. This is a geometric ONE-slot identification, not merely a continuous determinant trace. Original nonreduced rank cannot be inserted after reduction: k[[t]][epsilon]/epsilon² has the same boundary as k[[t]] but parameter lengths 2N versus N. Artifact: sections/n8.tex.

notes.text:
In a finite tower, B⊗_R K_P=product_Q L_Q gives d_P(F)=sum_Q[L_Q:K_P]dim_LQ(F⊗_B L_Q). CLOSED residue degrees multiply along centre towers. These are the componentwise geometric projection laws, including inseparability, missing components and varying degrees.

Normal-domain unnormalized traces compose on EVERY support by grouping embeddings in a common finite normal closure; inseparable multiplicities multiply. Dense tests and finite decreasing sums extend kernel equality to C/D. General conductor-admissible towers require BOTH intermediate admissibilities. Normalize each dominating source component: the integral closure of B/Q in L_Q equals that of R/P in L_Q by integrality transitivity, contains the base normalization, and its closed centres partition under localization. Incomparability identifies precisely the dominating component chains. Full-support normal field trace transitivity therefore identifies the direct composite tuple with the iterated tuple on EVERY normal centre and support, including lower-dimensional ones. Intermediate descent makes that tuple full-fibre constant; uniqueness proves direct descent and trace equality. Direct admissibility alone is insufficient.

Reduced finite-flat norms are transitive by field norm identities on every minimal base field and reduced generic-to-global polynomial equality. At nonminimal supports, flatness identifies the second algebra's maximal-ideal-layer quotients with first-layer quotients tensor its residue algebra. A first Artinian length multiplies every second residue length, exactly the direct kernel lengths. Dense moments and finite decreasing sums prove full trace towers.

Normalized towers fail in EVERY characteristic: A=k[[t]], B=A×A, F=A×k[[s]], with second map t=s². The field degree is two, including characteristic two, by Laurent exponent parity. Direct weights are (1,2)/3, successive normalized weights (1,1)/2. At (0,−1) the values are −2/3 and −1/2; unnormalized traces both equal −2.

Several arbitrary traced slots fail even flat. For the regular threefold R, B=R×R, H=(−1,0), V=(0,−1), each source arity-two product has a zero slot and is zero. But tau H=tau V=−1 and mu_R(−1,−1) has mass one; separately normalized traces give mass 1/4. Thus the ONE-slot restriction is essential.

For primary base change, t(v)=v_a(b), T(v)=v/t(v), potentials divide by t and mu_b=T_*[t mu_a], exactly ONE measure factor. For a separate source primary c, lambda(w)=w(aB), rho_c(w)=w|R/lambda, and pulled potentials are lambda·u∘rho_c. Then rho_c,*[lambda mu_B,c]=rho_a,*mu_B,aB on corresponding homogeneous tuples. The synchronized arbitrary trace slot is H_c(w)/lambda(w); its trace must use that rescaled slot. No lambda^(n−1) appears. Raw competitor sets transport by the same order bijection. Nonprimary gauges retain only their positive-finite partial domains.
